parsed.explanation: Nothing in the dossier documents a trans-specific exposure: no cross-dressing or impersonation offence, no border or marker practice, no facility, custody or care rule, and the only morality statute (Penal Code ss.153–155) reaches male same-sex acts, is unenforced, and has produced no reported prosecution. A recognised Pinapinaaine/Binabinaaine gender role gives the visitor a legible cultural category, and the state voted to retain the SOGI Expert mandate and is considering SOGI anti-discrimination law. Against that, no protection operates for gender identity outside employment, the constitutional grounds list is closed, the 2015 'no discrimination' observation is a decade stale, and no post-2015 climate data exists. Thin-data silence is not safety here, and the dormant 14-year penalty is a residual ceiling on the worst case. Rated a step below acceptance-with-working-protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No entry screening, gender-marker rule, or document-mismatch practice is sourced for this jurisdiction.
entry_documents.interaction: Whether a document discrepancy at a port could escalate into questioning or referral is unrecorded; the border stage is an open question, not a documented restraint.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No detention of a trans or LGB visitor is documented. Sections 153–155 carry 5–14 years but the 2015 report records no prosecutions and no later enforcement evidence exists.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No legal-aid, consular-access or custody-placement practice is described.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Unknown whether an ID or presentation query could feed into the dormant sexual-offence provisions; no documented pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No ward, shelter, cell-placement or single-sex facility rule for trans people appears anywhere in the record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility conduct cannot be assessed; the dossier states only that no subnational variation is recorded and none is named.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No refusal of care, medication seizure or gender-affirming-care restriction is sourced for visitors or residents.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or pharmacy contact as an outing route is unaddressed by the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No law frames gender expression as deception, impersonation or immorality; the sole morality statute targets male same-sex conduct and is unenforced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Delegation voted to retain the SOGI Independent Expert mandate (2016) and told the UPR it was considering SOGI anti-discrimination legislation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State posture is permissive-by-silence rather than protective; the criminalising sections remain on the books and unresponsive to decriminalisation calls.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule touching a trans minor traveller, guardian consent, schooling or guardianship is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: Marriage Act age-16 floor and family rules are general, not gender-identity measures; no minor-specific exposure can be derived.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The 2015 report recorded no societal discrimination or violence, but the dossier bars treating that as current; one uncited claim of violence against lesbians is unresolved and not carried.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime provision, complaint body or police-protection practice is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: With no recourse machinery, a visitor's report would land in an undocumented system; a traditional gender role may soften reception but is cultural, not legal.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity non-discrimination law; Article 15(3) lists race, origin, political opinion, colour and creed only; employment protection names sexual orientation, not gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Employment and Industrial Relations Code 2015 Art.107(2)(b) covers sexual orientation in employment — resident-facing and poorly enforced per 2015.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Outside employment the visitor has no statutory remedy; whether the contemplated SOGI bill passed is unresolved and cannot be credited.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register denies entry and excludes visibly trans visitors as routine state practice. This dossier documents no border refusal, no register, no exclusion and no enforcement at all, so it sits materially higher than the 0.35 tier.

Kestrel Isles documents secondary screening, refused admission and humiliating searches for trans travellers. Here those stages are simply unsourced — open questions, which the rubric weighs far lighter than documented friction — placing this jurisdiction above 0.55.

Meridia documents trained border officers, tribunal appeals, counsel and compensation, alongside brief detention. This dossier documents no operative remedy for gender identity outside employment, so it falls below 0.75 despite comparable absence of criminalisation of expression.

Brindleport enforces identity-based housing, shelter-placement and anti-discrimination rules with fines and reinstatement. No such enforced protection exists here; the resort to a traditional cultural role is a climate signal, not a working remedy, so the gap is wide.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime shows no trans-facing restriction at any journey stage: no expression offence, no border, facility, custody or care rule, and a dormant same-sex statute with no prosecutions on record. That is offset by the absence of any working protection — the constitutional grounds list is closed, employment protection omits gender identity, and no complaint mechanism is documented — and by a social record frozen at 2015. A recognised gender-diverse cultural role makes the visitor legible and lowers friction, while the unenforced 5–14 year provision sets a theoretical worst case if a trans woman's relationship were ever prosecuted. With thin data on entry, custody and care, the rating sits a step below acceptance-with-working-protections rather than at it.
